name: Non-syndromic anorectal malformation without fistula

criteria.description: Absence of a normal anal opening at birth
No evidence of fistulous tract connecting rectum to urogenital tract or perineum
Radiologic imaging confirming blind-ending rectum without fistula

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent anal opening and no fistula confirmed clinically and/or radiologically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical at birth; imaging supports classification and surgical planning.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Failure to pass meconium within 24 hours of birth
searchTerms: not passing first stool within 24 hours

common.symptomName: Constipation or absence of stool passage

common.notes: May be observed on physical exam
searchTerms: underdeveloped area between genitals and anus

occasional.notes: Rarely associated with spinal cord involvement
Secondary to urinary stasis or anomalies

rare.notes: Due to associated spinal cord anomalies
searchTerms: bladder control issues from nerve damage
inability to control bowel after surgery
loss of bowel control after repair

laboratory: Normal blood counts and metabolic panel unless complications arise
imaging: Abdominal and pelvic X-ray showing absence of distal rectal air column
Contrast distal colostogram confirming blind-ending rectum without fistula
Ultrasound to assess associated renal anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified in isolated cases
Genetic testing recommended if syndromic features present
other: Physical examination revealing absent anal opening and perineal anatomy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of fistulous tract connecting rectum to urogenital or perineal structures
Abnormal passage of stool via fistula
Delayed passage of meconium due to aganglionosis
Confirmed by rectal biopsy showing absence of ganglion cells

redFlags: Failure to identify any anal opening at birth
Signs of bowel obstruction such as abdominal distension and bilious vomiting
Associated urinary retention or spinal anomalies indicating complex malformations
references: Levitt MA, Peña A. Anorectal malformations. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007;2:33.

Holschneider A, Hutson J, Peña A, et al. Preliminary report on the International Conference for the Development of Standards for the Treatment of Anorectal Malformations. J Pediatr Surg. 2005;40(10):1521-1526.
Orphanet: Non-syndromic anorectal malformation without fistula (ORPHA:601002)
